Dry season: mid-February to mid-May [1]. April 2026: the DNP reported 11,419.75 rai damaged across 326 sites, as of 22 April [4]. Officials suspect arson linked to land clearing and illegal hunting; investigations continue [5][6]

Dusky Langur

Trachypithecus obscurus[10]

Lives in the canopy. Tree damage may reduce food and cover.

Asian Barred Owlet

Glaucidium cuculoides[10]

Uses trees to roost and nest. Fire may damage those sites.

Black-naped Monarch

Hypothymis azurea[9]

Nests low in the forest. Ground fires could destroy nests.

Leopard & black leopard

Panthera pardus[1][9]

Needs prey and forest cover. Habitat loss may affect both.

Elephant and tiger, both endangered

Elephas maximus · Panthera tigris[1][3]

Fire may reduce food and push animals to move.

Potential impacts, not proven effects of every fire. Species names to be confirmed with photo captions
